title: I Let the Software License Popup Apply to the Boss's Install

parts.text: I found a cracked installer on a USB labeled backups in the boss's drawer. I am thirty-three, IT, restraint on a good day. The boss, Pat, had just mailed a fear memo about piracy. The USB smelled faintly of the granola he always spills. Our actual license portal showed unused seats. He wanted cracked because the portal took clicks. Pat said, "That's my personal backup" I said, "It launches a keygen" I plugged it into a sandboxed VM like a professional gremlin. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again. My socks had a hole I had been ignoring since Tuesday, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The keygen window is on the VM, and his piracy memo is still in everyone's inbox.

parts.text: I sent Pat the license portal link and a screenshot of unused seats, not the keygen. I also sent InfoSec the USB because that is the job. Pat called it a witch hunt. InfoSec called it a write-up. The memo stayed, which was funny. We used the paid seats. The granola kept spilling. I labeled a new drawer USB: ACTUAL BACKUPS. He does not laugh at that. I do, quietly, in the server closet that smells like warm dust. Clicks are cheaper than cracked pride. InfoSec said, "Did you run it on prod" I said, "VM only" A junior admin asked if I was scared. I said I was employed. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i.
